prior_assessment_science_preserved.context: The original proof and finite checks remain in the pinned source-tree Git history. The earlier originality rationale omitted the October 13 same-object exact negative cherry–Wiener theorem; this repair credits its scalar consequences and narrows novelty to the shellwise theorem.
prior_assessment_science_preserved.correctness_original_rationale: Uniform Cayley forest extension yields the fixed marked-pair distance mass, and cherry deletion gives the exact Palm law and covariance. The sign identity reduces to a strictly log-concave ratio for shell indices 3..n-2; n>=8 endpoints and n=4..7 exact values establish one crossing. Expansion at t sqrt(n) proves the sharp limit, and summation-by-parts proves monotone-cost negativity. Independently enumerated all 18,244 Cayley trees of size 4..7 and checked rational formulas through n=200.
prior_assessment_science_preserved.originality_original_rationale: No direct exact cherry-vs-all-pairs-distance profile covariance or sharp sqrt(2n) sign classification was identified in accessible comparison sources; nearest leaf-vs-distance and cherry-vs-leaf results have different joint events. A structurally motivated but not independently certified historical-priority risk remains.
prior_assessment_science_preserved.value_original_rationale: Cherries measure local terminal branching while all-pairs distance is a global shape observable. The proof supplies every distance-shell covariance, its unique sharp size-dependent sign reversal near sqrt(2n), and universal negative covariance against any strictly increasing distance cost, a structural result exceeding a known marginal count or a routine small example.

scope: Uniform labeled unrooted unweighted Cayley trees for n>=4; exact finite shell covariance, unique crossing, sqrt(2n) cutoff, monotone distance cost consequence; scalar cherry–Wiener result credited to October 2026 prior work.
